title: Steph Curry returns to Warriors in regular form, nearly knocks off red-hot Rockets
content:
SAN FRANCISCO — Easter isn’t the only religious holiday some members of the Golden State Warriors organization observed Sunday night. They also celebrated the return of the most important figure in the team’s history: Stephen Curry. The 38-year-old superstar was back after missing the last two months with a right knee injury and scored 29 points in 26 minutes. He missed a potential game-winning 3 at the buzzer in a 117-116 loss to the Houston Rockets.

After shaking off some understandable rust following such a long layoff, Curry, who came off the bench for the first time in a regular-season game since 2012, went 11-for-21 from the field and 5-for-10 from beyond the arc. He got more comfortable as the game wore on and seemed to be moving around fine.

“I felt good,” Curry said. “Some good nerves going into it. And obviously coming off the bench you’re trying to pace yourself, physically, mentally, to get ready for your runs. The first run was tough, the second one was great, the second quarter once I got my feet underneath me. Obviously, the momentum carried, all the work you put in in rehab to get through even 26 minutes at that level, I was very grateful for sure.”

Curry wore a large heating pack around the knee to keep it loose on the bench and acknowledged trying to do a little too much early in the game in an attempt to find his rhythm. Curry received a standing ovation after checking in for the first time with 4:54 left in the first quarter and electrified the crowd in the second half by knocking down the types of long range shots that have defined his career.

His return created a buzz throughout the sold out Chase Center and gave the Warriors, who have just four regular season games left and have been locked into the Play-In Tournament for weeks, a big emotional lift.

“You can just feel it,” Kerr said of having Curry back. “We’re back in the mix. We’re back in the fight with Steph and that’s a hell of a team, they’ve been really hot lately, and fully healthy, and we took them down to the last shot.”

Curry acknowledged after Saturday’s practice that with the season winding down, he pushed hard to make it back after sitting for 27 games because of how much he missed the game and wanted to help his teammates. As he reflected both before and after the game, Curry expressed gratitude for being able to play on the NBA stage again.

“It’s Easter Sunday,” Curry said. “Resurrection Sunday, this has been a special day to reflect and appreciate what I get to do on a daily basis, the gift God’s given me to be healthy, fight through this rehab stint and be able to get back to the court and enjoy myself. There were a lot of nerves all day. My family supported me at home when I was a nervous wreck trying to pass the hours before I got to the arena. But once you get back to your routine, you’ve been doing it so long, muscle memory takes over, the adrenaline takes over. I appreciate the fans and the reception, just the buzz that was in the arena, cause you know at a certain point you won’t be able to tap into that.”

Curry admitted on Saturday that he has to face a “new normal” as far as his knee is concerned. He has done all the rehab work he can do, but there remains a chance the pain could return. As far as his first test back, Curry passed with flying colors, according to Kerr. The Warriors enjoyed having their leader back on the floor, knowing he can lift them up when they are down.

“I don’t think there’s a tougher defender in the league for him to have his first game against than Amen Thompson,” Kerr said. “So that’s quite a test. Steph looked amazing. He’s worked really hard for this. You can see it doesn’t take much for him to find his rhythm. And his rhythm is also our rhythm. All the off-ball stuff that we get as a result of his movement.”

Curry, who was on a minutes restriction Sunday, expects to be right around 25 minutes again Tuesday night against the Sacramento Kings.

The highlight for Curry on Sunday came when he was finally able to share the floor with his brother, Seth, for the first time in an NBA game. The siblings have battled different injuries throughout the season but were finally able to play together in Game 77 of the season.

“It was a great moment,” Seth Curry said. “Great moment. Just to be out there on the same floor for the first time since high school was special for us, special for the family.”

While the Curry brothers shared a special family moment, Bay Area fans rejoiced on Sunday as their favorite son returned to doing what he does best. Kerr summed it up in describing what Curry’s return meant to the rest of the group.

“There’s just a momentum and a confidence,” Kerr said. “He’s Steph Curry for a reason.”
